text:
incident-bot: [SECURITY NOTICE] auth-gateway abnormal header logging pattern detected. Multiple uploads to s3://redwood-logs/auth-verbose-headers/ containing request headers. Potential exposure of Authorization headers. Paging sec-oncall and infra oncall.
alex (oncall): acknowledged, grabbing the page. Anyone seeing customer errors or just the log artifacts? :wave:
priya: auth gateway 401s up ~9% in last 7m for oauth flows. A couple of enterprise customers reported session drops. No 5xx.
sam: I pulled a sample object from the bucket and see lines like `Authorization: Bearer eyJ...` with truncation in the middle but prefix and suffix present. Could be used to infer token if attacker reconstructs. We should assume compromise for affected tokens.
alex (oncall): treat as sensitive. sec-oncall, recommend immediate containment: block write access to that bucket, remove files, rotate credentials, revoke sessions.
sec-oncall: joining. Labeling incident security/token-exposure. Immediate plan: 1) disable the logging path in the gateway config 2) quarantine S3 objects to secure bucket 3) rotate oauth client secrets and service keys 4) force token revocation and blacklist earlier tokens 5) prepare customer notifications for impacted customers. I'll coordinate rotation and revocation.
pagerduty: Created PD-9123. Oncall ack: alex (oncall).
ops-bot: starting rollback: pipeline #4910 rollback to previous release (removing verbose header logging).
priya: rollback applied, new pods not writing header dumps. Running `aws s3 ls` to enumerate recent objects:

```
$ aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs/auth-verbose-headers/ --recursive
2026-03-16 02:12:08   20480 auth-headers/2026-03-16-02-11-50.dump
2026-03-16 01:58:00    7680 auth-headers/2026-03-16-01-57-22.dump
```

sam: copying identified objects to s3://redwood-secure-archive/2115801234/ for forensics (checksum preserved) then deleting originals.
ops-bot: s3 copy job succeeded. originals scheduled for deletion.
alex (oncall): rotation plan — who can rotate oauth client secrets for `oauth-gateway-client`? Need to rotate now and push new secret via sealed-secrets.
sec-oncall: I'll perform rotation. Steps: generate new client secret, update vault, push sealed-secret, restart gateway, and apply token policy to reject pre-rotation tokens. I'll aim for minimal disruption.
sam: commands (internal reference):

```
# create new secret
vault kv put secret/oauth-clients/oauth-gateway-client client_secret=<NEW_SECRET>
# update sealed-secret
kubectl -n auth set secret oauth-gateway-client --from-literal=client_secret=<NEW_SECRET>
kubectl rollout restart deployment/oauth-gateway
```

priya: kicking restart now.
ops-bot: rollout started: deployment/oauth-gateway (replicas: 4)
sec-oncall: applying runtime guard: reject tokens with `iat` before 2026-03-16T02:15:00Z. Also adding an audit flag `token_revoke=true` to all revoke events.
priya: monitoring auth traffic — 401 rate starting to decline after rollout and revocations.
csk (csm): I've notified two enterprise customers directly via secure channel; one asked whether they need to rotate their app secret — advising re-issue if they store long-lived tokens. Drafting brief for status page and targeted emails.
alex (oncall): add WAF blocks for suspicious IPs observed in header upload requests. Priya, can you identify top offender IPs?
priya: top offenders: 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/25. Applying temporary deny rules now.
ops-bot: WAF rules applied: deny lists added for 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/25.
sam: forensic checklist: capture CI pipeline #4910 logs, k8s audit events for the merge and rollout, git commit and PR metadata (feature/log-headers), and S3 object metadata. Save chain of custody for deleted objects.
sec-oncall: noted. I will preserve forensics in redwood-secure-archive and restrict access to sec+incident responders.
ops-bot: s3 delete job completed for originals. forensic copies remain in s3://redwood-secure-archive/2115801234/ (access: sec-team).
alex (oncall): summary of actions: disabled verbose header logging (rollback), quarantined artifacts (copied & deleted), rotated oauth client secret and restarted gateway, blacklisted tokens issued before rotation time, applied WAF blocks, notified impacted customers. Postmortem owner: sam. Follow-up: tighten CI PR checks to prevent header-logging flags in prod branches.
sec-oncall: marking containment achieved. We'll retain incident active until postmortem and customer communications go out. Also scheduling rotation of any service keys that may have been logged (list to be determined from objects).
csk (csm): preparing customer advisory: short, non-alarming, recommend re-login and rotation for customers that use static credentials. Will send to sec-oncall for review before publishing.
alex (oncall): handoff to night oncall @sam (oncall) at 2115801960. Sam will monitor auth metrics, WAF hit rates, and any customer escalations. Escalate to sec immediately for any token replay evidence.
sec-oncall: agreed. We'll also run an audit tomorrow to identify any other buckets or services with similar logging flags. Create JIRA for CI pipeline hardening and PR checklist updates.
alex (oncall): closing active pager for this shift. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
